title: Withdraw raw subject analytics and entry payload logs
scope: Bounded W07 future-write containment: withdraw eight subject-bearing AE writes in tracking, pixel, webhook and Optimizely routers; remove blanket request URL and raw queue payload/error logs at the Worker entry, and raw error objects in those routers and global error middleware. Preserve dispatcher/Optimizely domain effects, response and queue semantics, health/ledger aggregate measurement. Correct erasure receipts for historical AE/log destinations without claiming deletion or full privacy acceptance.
non_goals: No scoring, ledger schema/producer/consumer, business dispatch, consent or route-auth policy, SDK, dataset/provisioning, retention or historical deletion change; no new replacement telemetry pipeline.

Other EventDispatcher/OptimizelyService/scene-generation/WebSocket/scheduled/route log paths and public error-response contents remain unaccepted W07 scope; no all-logs-clean, nothing-written-under-refusal, full erasure/W07/finding/gate/customer/SLO/release or earlier-proof reclosure claim.
No real network, deployment/cloud/resource/credential/customer-data operations, operational scripts, staging/commit/push, cleanup, broad test framework or unrelated changes.

criteria.description: All eight actual mounted route writers never access AE with absent/throwing bindings, including synthetic refused-consent input. Existing dispatcher/Optimizely effects, successful response shapes, batch continuation and pixel success/error GIF/cache behavior survive; malformed input retains existing responses. Health and ledger aggregate writes remain unchanged. Historical AE and logs are unconditionally named notReached after existing ODP without changing erasure operations or promising retention/deletion.

Actual Worker entry requests with synthetic path/query/request-ID data emit no blanket URL logs; default queue bodies, scene result fields, ledger failure detail and queue catch error contents are not logged at index sites, preserving acknowledgements/retries. Selected router and global error logs use fixed labels only; response/error and residual service log limits are explicit.

Independent frozen source/baseline/assertion/evidence review and targeted K1/K2 reruns, inspected actual application noEmit and relevant source/config/lock/proof identity confirm bounded remediation and protected prior changes; no duplicate broad matrix or full application/runtime attestation.
